get.summary: Returns data inputs for certain index definition and time
Returns all data inputs for a specific index definition
Current Index Values for index definition
Historical Index Values for index definition

parameters.name: period_id
parameters.description: Identifier of requested timeseries period (e.g. `5SEC` or `1DAY`)

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Amount of items to return (optional, mininum is 1, maximum is 100000, default value is 100, if the parameter is used then every 100 output items are counted as one request)

get.description:
Get a detailed list of exchanges provided by the system.
            
:::info
Properties of the output are providing aggregated information from across all symbols related to the specific exchange. If you need to calculate your aggregation (e.g., limiting only the particular type of symbols), you should use /v1/symbols endpoint as a data source.
:::

parameters.name: filter_exchange_id
parameters.description: Comma or semicolon delimited exchange identifiers used to filter response. (optional, eg. `BITSTAMP;GEMINI`)

parameters.name: time
parameters.description: Optional - when given, only weights valid at that time are returned

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Optional - when given, only weights valid at or after that time are returned (cannot be combined with time)

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: Optional - when given, only weights valid before that time are returned (cannot be combined with time)

get.description:
Get full list of supported time periods
            
### Available periods
            
Time unit | Period identifiers
--------- | -----------
Second | 1SEC, 2SEC, 3SEC, 4SEC, 5SEC, 6SEC, 10SEC, 15SEC, 20SEC, 30SEC
Minute | 1MIN, 2MIN, 3MIN, 4MIN, 5MIN, 6MIN, 10MIN, 15MIN, 20MIN, 30MIN
Hour | 1HRS, 2HRS, 3HRS, 4HRS, 6HRS, 8HRS, 12HRS
Day | 1DAY, 2DAY, 3DAY, 5DAY, 7DAY, 10DAY
Month | 1MTH, 2MTH, 3MTH, 4MTH, 6MTH
Year | 1YRS, 2YRS, 3YRS, 4YRS, 5YRS
            
:::tip
You can assume that we will not remove any periods from this response, however, we may add new ones.
:::

validFrom.description: Start of validity (inclusive), null means unbounded

time_period_start.description: Gets or sets the start time of the time period.

time_period_end.description: Gets or sets the end time of the time period.

time_open.description: Gets or sets the time when the value opened.

time_close.description: Gets or sets the time when the value closed.

value_open.description: Gets or sets the opening value.

value_high.description: Gets or sets the highest value during the time period.

value_low.description: Gets or sets the lowest value during the time period.

value_close.description: Gets or sets the closing value.

value_count.description: Gets or sets the number of values during the time period.
